sampling.method: For each event class pull_request, merge_group and push, select the two most recent completed META CI runs returned by the event-filtered GitHub Actions runs endpoint at the observation cutoff. Selection is not filtered by conclusion.
sampling.scope: Oteryn/Oteryn META CI only; recent trigger-stratified operational sample, not a statistically representative long-term workload sample.

proven.trigger_stratification: The bounded sample contains exactly two recent completed META CI runs for each of pull_request, merge_group and push.
proven.sample_outcomes: All six sampled meta-gate jobs concluded success and all six sampled workflow runs have run_attempt=1.
proven.observed_created_to_start_delay: Within this sample, job created-to-start delay is 2-3 seconds (median 2 seconds). This is a timestamp interval only, not pure queue time.
proven.observed_execution: Within this sample, meta-gate start-to-completion is 10-13 seconds (median 12 seconds).
proven.runner_allocation: The six jobs report ubuntu-latest and six distinct GitHub-hosted runner IDs; this proves distinct observed allocations only, not fleet capacity.
proven.workflow_cache_configuration: The bound ci.yml has no explicit actions/cache step. GitHub Actions metadata collected here does not expose cache hit/miss or provider-level package-cache behavior.
proven.verification_yield_proxy: The six successful jobs expose 33 successful named Check/Validate steps in authoritative job metadata. The packet records only the count; source job IDs are the recheck authority. This is a bounded execution-count proxy, not proof of defect-detection value or economic efficiency.

unknown_or_blocked.billing_cost: UNKNOWN: collected run/job metadata does not include authoritative billed minutes, spend or marginal cost.
unknown_or_blocked.runner_capacity: UNKNOWN: short created-to-start delays and distinct runner IDs do not expose available fleet capacity, saturation or concurrency headroom.
unknown_or_blocked.cache_efficiency: UNKNOWN: no authoritative cache hit/miss, transferred-byte or cache-time telemetry was collected.
unknown_or_blocked.flake_rate: UNKNOWN: six recent successful runs are too small and too short a window to establish a long-term flake rate.
unknown_or_blocked.retry_rate: UNKNOWN beyond the sampled run IDs: each sampled run is attempt 1, but this cohort does not establish organization-wide retry frequency.
unknown_or_blocked.cost_savings: UNKNOWN: no baseline-vs-current billable usage or spend dataset is available.
unknown_or_blocked.useful_verification_yield: PARTIAL: named successful validation steps are observable, but prevented defects, redundant work and value per billed minute are not.
unknown_or_blocked.pure_queue_time: UNKNOWN: job created-to-start delay does not identify when the job became runnable or when a runner was assigned, so pure queue time is not measured.

limitations: This is a trigger-stratified six-run META sample from one day, not a statistically representative long-term workload sample.
GitHub Actions run/job metadata is sufficient for bounded timestamps and attempt numbers but not authoritative billing cost, fleet capacity or cache efficiency.
Job created-to-start delay is an observed timestamp interval, not pure queue time; runnable and runner-assignment timestamps are unavailable in this evidence.
The absence of an explicit actions/cache step does not prove that no runner-level or package-manager cache behavior occurred.
A successful run does not prove every validation step had equal usefulness, nor that equivalent validation was not repeated elsewhere.
COST-CI remains open; no cost-savings, queue-health, pure-queue-time, runner-capacity, cache-efficiency or flake-rate claim is established.

smallest_additional_observation.cohort_cost_cache: Obtain authoritative billable execution/usage for these exact six run IDs plus cache hit/miss (or explicit proof that no cache telemetry exists). This would permit bounded per-cohort cost/cache statements.
smallest_additional_observation.generalized_efficiency: For any long-term flake/capacity/efficiency claim, collect an unfiltered rolling cohort covering both successful and unsuccessful/retried runs across a materially longer window, then bind billing and queue telemetry to the same run IDs.

recheck_triggers: Any selected run/job identity, timestamp, attempt or conclusion no longer matches authoritative GitHub readback.
Authoritative billing/usage or cache telemetry becomes available for the sampled run IDs.
A larger rolling cohort is collected for a long-term efficiency or flake/capacity claim.
